name: TotK Recomp
cost: Free (MIT for the project's code). You need your own copy of the game
works_with: Windows 10 or later and Linux (including Steam Deck), x86-64 with a Vulkan 1.3 GPU
short: Rebuilds Tears of the Kingdom from your own game files as a native Windows or Linux app, with Vulkan, high frame rates and mod support.
what: TotK Recomp is a static recompilation of The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom into native x86-64 code, so no emulator is involved. A setup program builds the game from your own files on your machine. It supports updates 1.1.0, 1.2.1 and 1.4.3, up to 144 fps (experimental), custom resolutions, FSR 1, DLSS on RTX cards, HDR10, ultrawide, gamepad remapping, and mods and cheats made for emulators.
who: Owners of the game who have dumped it from their own console and want to play on a PC or Steam Deck. It is in early development, so expect visual bugs and crashes. No game files are included and the project won't tell you how to get them.
needs: Your own dump of Tears of the Kingdom: the base game and the 1.1.0, 1.2.1 or 1.4.3 update
About 36 GiB free during setup (20 GiB after)
On Linux: kernel 6.7 or later and glibc 2.34 or later

steps.title: Windows: download the setup
steps.text: Download `TotK-Setup-<version>-windows.zip` from Releases and unpack it. Start `TotK-Setup.exe`.

steps.title: Linux: download the setup
steps.text: Download `TotK-Setup-x86_64.AppImage` from Releases. On a Steam Deck, do this in Desktop Mode.

steps.title: Build the game
steps.text: Pick your game files, the language and an install folder, and press Start. The setup builds the game once.

steps.title: Play
steps.text: Run `totk.exe` (Windows) or `totk` (Linux) from the install folder. F1 opens settings and F10 the performance overlay. To update, run a newer setup on the same folder; saves and settings are kept.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Open the in-game settings with F1, turn on DLSS or FSR, and try a higher frame rate. Mods made for emulators go in the `mods` folder next to `totk.exe`.

watch: The built game contains the game itself. The README says it is for your own use and not to share it.
The Windows setup is unsigned, so SmartScreen will warn you.
With an NVIDIA RTX GPU the setup downloads `nvngx_dlss.dll` from NVIDIA's DLSS SDK repository unless you untick Download NVIDIA DLSS.
Discord Rich Presence is off by default.
Early development: the game is playable, but visual bugs and crashes are expected.
